paper.title: A computational linguistic methodology for assessing semiotic structure in prehistoric art and the meaning of southern Scandinavian Mesolithic ornamentation
paper.citation: Herskind, L.L.P., Riede, F., 2024. Journal of Archaeological Science 165, 105969. Available online 3 April 2024.

eligibility.notes: Authors: Lasse Lukas Platz Herskind and Felix Riede (Aarhus University); the study registrant Shawn Ross is not an author. Code: Herskind&Riede_S2.R (759 lines, UTF-8, CRLF line endings), one R script in 8 PARTs that reads S1 and produces Fig. 2 (bar panel), Table 1, Table 2, Fig. 3, the Fig. 4 skeleton, and the S3 tables. No random numbers anywhere, so the run is fully deterministic. Estimated compute: image build 0.5-1 h (binary packages from Posit Package Manager for the rocker jammy base), script run a few minutes, so about 1.5 h in total against the 168 h cap. No API calls or paid services. Tolerance instrument verdicts-and-precision.md v1.1 read in full (Receipt-token 46eb4ad0bfcb3b92). The agent brief's pulled references verification-strategies.md and pilot-reproduction-summary.md are on the blinded list, so they were skipped and are not declared. BLINDING DISCLOSURE: while looking for the run-container entry point I ran an ls of /home/shawn/Code/llm-reproducibility/reproduction-system/ that was filtered only for 'workflows'. Its output printed the blinded filename lodged-rules.yaml. That file was not opened, read, searched, or otherwise accessed, and none of its content was seen; the lodged rules were quoted only from the spawn prompt. Reported for the approver's ruling on admissibility (see questions_for_approver).

reproduction_type.rationale: The authors supply one annotated R script (S2.R) written to be run interactively ('run the code all at once ... or go through it one line at a time'). There is no container or lockfile, but README.txt states R 4.3.2 and seven package versions. Statement 27 (extrafont::font_import for the proprietary Gill Sans MT font) produces an error the authors note and ignore, so an unwrapped Rscript run may halt there. Plots are autoprinted, Tables 1 and 2 were copied by hand from console output into Word, and Figs. 3 and 4 were finished in GIMP. Fig. 2's map, Fig. 5, and Table 3 have no code at all. The computational core runs top to bottom in batch once a wrapper adds mechanics only: working directory, graphics device, per-expression error capture, and a declared tolerance for statement 27. Risk assessment: low compute risk, a deterministic pipeline, and moderate build risk (seven pinned CRAN versions on R 4.3.2). The main scoring risks are the code-less targets that need verification aids, and visual comparison of figures assembled outside R.

plan.compute_strategy: All builds and runs happen on this machine through the run-container procedure named in the run notes (I did not locate a script by that name under scripts/ or reproduction-system/runtime/, so the executor uses the project's standard run-container entry point). Step 1: build one image from rocker/r-ver:4.3.2 with the seven README-pinned packages and the 2024-04-03 snapshot for everything else; record the digest, sessionInfo(), and installed.packages(). Step 2: one serial container run of the wrapper run-analysis.R, with the deposit mounted read-only, no network, and LANG=en_US.UTF-8. Step 3: the comparison script (compare.R, containing the labelled verification aids) runs in the same image, against the run's snapshots and the published values. Expected wall-clock is under 2 h (build-dominated); the script itself takes minutes, there is no RNG, and nothing is parallelised because nothing needs to be. Conservative default flagged: serial build and run. Parallel package compilation (Ncpus) could shorten the build if PPM binaries are unavailable, but it is not needed within the cap.

execution_steps.action: Retrieve the four Zenodo v2 files (S1.xlsx, S2.R, S3.xlsx, README.txt) by anonymous REST API into the attempt's materials directory; verify each md5 against Zenodo's published checksums; record sha256; log route, steps, and outcome per dataset for L-level assignment.

execution_steps.action: Write the Dockerfile: FROM rocker/r-ver:4.3.2; point the CRAN repo at the PPM snapshot 2024-04-03; install remotes; remotes::install_version for the seven README pins; install fontconfig and DejaVu fonts; set LANG=en_US.UTF-8. Build through run-container. On a build failure, apply the version-search cap (pin, preceding release, following release) and log each attempt.

execution_steps.action: Write the wrapper run-analysis.R (mechanics only, never inside the authors' file). It: copies S1 to a working directory and sets it as wd; sets the default graphics device to a file-based cairo PNG so autoprinted plots never hit the pdf font database; parses S2.R unchanged (sha256 checked before and after); evaluates top-level expressions in the authors' order in the global environment with per-expression error and warning capture, printing visible values as autoprint would; maps each expression to its PART by srcref line; declares an error tolerance only for statement 27 (extrafont::font_import, font registration that enters no result) and logs whether it fired; records PART completion status; saves an RDS snapshot of the global environment at the end of each PART and an RDS list of all visible values.
execution_steps.expected_output: run-analysis.R; a declared-tolerance list containing only S2.R line 27.

execution_steps.action: Run the wrapper in the container via run-container, with no network and the deposit read-only.
execution_steps.expected_output: outputs/: artefact_type_chronology.png, bigramsBYfrequency.png, bigramsBYpmi.png, trigramsBYfrequency.png, trigramsBYpmi.png, quadrigramsBYfrequency.png, quadrigramsBYpmi.png, heatmapPMI.png, Bigrams.csv, Trigrams.csv, Quadrigrams.csv; console log; per-PART status table (P1-P8 completed or failed, with errors); per-PART snapshots; visible-values RDS; tolerance-fired log for line 27.

execution_steps.action: Deterministic stage gate: S2.R byte-identical after the run; every expected artefact exists and is non-empty; record PART completion status; derive each target's credit eligibility from the Q6 dependency map (T01: P1,P3,P4; T02: P1,P3,P5; T04: P1,P2; T05: P1,P3,P5,P6; T06: P1,P3,P5,P6,P7; T08: P1,P3,P5,P6,P7,P8; aid targets: the PARTs whose objects they read).

execution_steps.action: Transcribe published values into machine-readable files, double-entered and diffed: Table 1 (130 values), Table 2 (18), Table 3 (50), the Fig. 3 bar labels and 4-dp PMI labels for all six panels (128 bars), the Fig. 4 axis order and boxed cells (count the small boxes in the published figure before any comparison), the Fig. 5 pie compositions, and the named values T09-T17. S3 is read directly from the deposited xlsx.

execution_steps.action: Write and run compare.R, kept separate from the authors' code. Its sections are: (a) code-produced targets T01, T02, T05, T08 and the T04 bar panel and T06 heatmap cells, compared from snapshots and outputs; (b) clearly labelled VERIFICATION AID blocks (R1/Q5) for T03, the T04 map, the T06 box overlay, T07, and T09-T17, using only read-only lookups in the authors' run objects (data, corpus, freqs, bigrams_subset, bigramsBYpmi$data, Part 7 bigrams) plus documented quanteda, dplyr, and ggplot2 functions, with the pre-stated rules given in the targets. Each inferred rule is first run on its printed-input qualification test. The script also runs a deterministic element-count gate per target (7c).
execution_steps.expected_output: compare.R; per-target comparison tables; element-count gate output (declared count against elements checked); aid outputs labelled as aids.

execution_steps.action: Write comparisons/comparison-report.md with per-target discrepancy categories, Q6 section-credit status, 7c partial-verification flags, R4 notes (log-base and t=482 text/code inconsistencies; the T13 list of eight against 'nine'), any PAPER_ERROR candidates with the evidence tier named (escalated for human confirmation), coverage = reproduced / 17, and the verdict. Then hand off to fresh-context adversarial review (invariant 4).

verification_targets.description: Frequency distributions of unigrams (individual motifs, n = 230), 13-skip-2-grams (n = 1543), 13-skip-3-grams (n = 4422) and 13-skip-4-grams (n = 8466): 63 (frequency, n) rows (31 unigram, 18 bigram, 9 trigram, 5 quadrigram) plus 4 header totals.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Execute S2.R unmodified through the wrapper. Part 4 (S2.R lines 222-264) outputs table(freqs) (presence columns data[,31:289], zero columns dropped), table(bigramfreqs), table(trigramfreqs), table(quadrigramfreqs), and the four length() totals; the wrapper captures them as visible values. Compare every (frequency, n) pair and the four totals with the double-entered transcription. Scope: the whole table, 130 values; a deterministic gate confirms 130 elements compared (7c). Credit only if PARTs 1, 3, and 4 complete without error (Q6; Part 4 reads data from P1 and corpus and k from P3). Planning check: the printed n columns sum to the printed headers (230, 1543, 4422, 8466).
verification_targets.tolerance: Deterministic, tolerance 0: each of the 130 integers must be EXACT_MATCH; any difference is a discrepancy (MAJOR_DISCREPANCY unless the 7(a) PAPER_ERROR protocol applies).

verification_targets.description: Summary statistics (maximum, 3rd quartile, mean, median, 1st quartile, minimum) of whole-corpus bigram PMI values for bigrams occurring in each culture complex (Maglemose, Kongemose, Ertebølle), observed frequency >= 3: 6 x 3 = 18 values at 2 dp.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Part 5 (S2.R lines 265-322) prints summary() of magle/konge/erte_ksngram_subset$PMI. The wrapper captures the full-precision summary objects; compare.R rounds them to 2 dp and maps Max., 3rd Qu., Mean, Median, 1st Qu., and Min. onto the table rows. Scope: all 18 cells; element gate 18 (7c). Credit only if PARTs 1, 3, and 5 complete (Q6). R4: the printed values are the scoring reference. The paper's formula says log2, but S2.R lines 174, 186, and 197 use natural log(), and t is hard-coded as 482 where the text defines t as the total number of objects. These text/code inconsistencies are reported and never used to rescore. If the reproduced values disagree with the printed ones, the 7(a) PAPER_ERROR protocol applies and the finding escalates. S3's bigram sheet is an additional cross-check of the underlying PMI values.
verification_targets.tolerance: Deterministic, printed to 2 dp: EXACT_MATCH when the reproduced value rounded to 2 dp equals the printed value; WITHIN_PRECISION when |reproduced - printed| <= 0.005 but rounding direction differs (half-up vs half-even); any larger difference is a discrepancy.

verification_targets.description: The ten objects in Fig. 5 bearing the most salient motif collocations: site, region, artefact type, motifs, and figure number in Płonka (2003) for each of 10 rows.
verification_targets.comparison_method: No authors' code produces Table 3. A labelled verification aid (R1/Q5) in compare.R does a read-only lookup in `data` (S1 as read by the authors' Part 1, from the P1 snapshot), matching each row by Site and Płonka figure number (S1 'Figure'). For each row it compares Region (S1 'Region'), artefact type (S1 'Material' + 'Artefact type'), the motif set (S1 'Motifs' slot columns P:AD, order-insensitive), and Figure. Scope: 10 rows x 5 columns = 50 values; element gate 50 (7c). Row number # is an index into Fig. 5 and is not scored. Credit only if PART 1 completes (Q6).
verification_targets.tolerance: Deterministic lookup, tolerance 0: EXACT_MATCH per cell after normalising whitespace, letter case, and quotation marks; motif lists compared as sets. Any other difference is a discrepancy.

verification_targets.description: Two panels. Left: horizontal bars of 18 artefact-type levels (axe ... slotted point, other) stacked by four chronology levels (Maglemose, Kongemose, Kongemose/Ertebølle, Ertebølle), x axis 0-100. Right: map of all South Scandinavian ornamented objects coloured by chronology.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Bar panel: produced by PART 2 (S2.R lines 33-75; ggsave artefact_type_chronology.png). Compare visually with the published panel for bar order, relative lengths against the 0-100 axis, and chronology composition, and report the counts behind the plot (table of Artefact_Type x Chronology from the authors' DS object). Map panel: README says the coordinate columns were used to produce the map, but S2.R contains no map code. A labelled verification aid (R1/Q5) plots Coord.Long/Coord.Lat from `data` with ggplot2::geom_point coloured by Chronology under coord_quickmap(), and the point distribution and colours are compared visually. Scope: 18 bars (up to 4 segments each) plus one point per S1 object with non-missing coordinates (count recorded at run); element gate on both (7c). Basemap, scale bar, and north arrow are excluded as non-data elements (see exclusions). Credit only if PARTs 1 and 2 complete (Q6).
verification_targets.tolerance: Visual (verdicts-and-precision v1.1: scientific content must match; no pixel matching). Bar order, relative lengths, and composition must match; map point pattern and chronology colours must match. Typeface (Gill Sans MT unavailable), projection, basemap, and layout are not scored. A difference caused only by an unpublished cartographic convention is MINOR_DISCREPANCY (R1).

verification_targets.description: Six panels of chronology-stacked bars with 4-dp PMI labels: (a) 21 most frequent bigrams (observed > 9); (b) 21 bigrams by highest PMI (observed > 2); (c) 23 most frequent trigrams (observed > 4); (d) 23 trigrams by highest PMI; (e) 20 most frequent quadrigrams (observed > 2); (f) 20 quadrigrams by highest PMI. 128 bars in total.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Produced by PART 6 (S2.R lines 323-625; ggsave lines 615-620); the panels were assembled in GIMP. From the six ggplot objects (bigramsBYfrequency ... quadrigramsBYpmi) compare.R extracts each panel's bar identities and order, the 4-dp PMI label strings (geom_text sprintf('%.4f')), and the stacked frequencies by chronology. Labels and orders are compared exactly with the transcription; stacked bar lengths are compared visually with the published panels. Scope: 6 panels, 128 bars, 128 PMI labels; element gate 128 (7c). Cross-check: all 128 skipgrams have observed frequency > 2, so S3 holds their PMI values. Credit only if PARTs 1, 3, 5, and 6 complete (Q6). R4 applies to the log-base text/code inconsistency as for T02: scored against the printed labels.
verification_targets.tolerance: Deterministic: the 128 PMI labels must be EXACT_MATCH as 4-dp strings; bar identity and order exact in every panel; stacked chronology frequencies are integers compared visually against the axis, and any visible difference is a discrepancy. GIMP assembly, typeface, and layout are not scored.
verification_targets.published_values_source: Paper text, Fig. 3 (p. 5) labels transcribed; deposit Herskind&Riede_S3.xlsx as a numeric cross-check

verification_targets.description: PMI heatmap of bigrams with observed frequency >= 3 over 49 motif tokens in the authors' manual chronological order (A14 ... RELIEF), red gradient (midpoint 0.5). A GIMP overlay adds small coloured boxes (purple Maglemose, red Kongemose, yellow Ertebølle) marking combinations limited to one culture complex, plus large boxes for culture-specific high-PMI groups (A14-A24; B10-F38; D33-H1; I5-I13; the C4/C5/C12/C13/D7 cluster) with motif pictograms.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Heatmap skeleton: PART 7 (S2.R lines 626-697; heatmapPMI.png). Compare visually for the 49-label axis order (exact) and the cell shading pattern; the cell PMI values (165 bigrams) are checked numerically against S3's bigram sheet. Box overlay: no code (added in GIMP). A labelled verification aid (R1/Q5) does a read-only lookup in `data` (dplyr::filter on the presence columns) of the Chronology values of objects bearing both motifs, for each of the 165 Part 7 bigrams. Pre-stated inferred rule: a cell carries a small box iff all such objects share exactly one of Maglemose, Kongemose, or Ertebølle, in that culture's colour; pairs involving any 'Kongemose/Ertebølle' object are expected unboxed. Qualification test (Q5): the rule is applied first to the bigrams whose chronology composition is printed in Fig. 3a/3b and must reproduce their published boxing; otherwise the overlay is not credited and goes to 7(a). Large boxes: check that every large-boxed pair is small-boxed in the stated culture, and report its PMI rank. Scope: 49 axis labels, 165 cells, every published small box (counted from the published figure before comparison), and 5 large boxes; element gate (7c). Pictograms are excluded as illustrations. Credit only if PARTs 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7 complete (Q6). R4 log-base note as T02.
verification_targets.tolerance: Visual for the colour gradient; exact for axis order, cell set, and box membership. A difference caused only by the unpublished treatment of 'Kongemose/Ertebølle' objects, or by the unpublished 'particularly high PMI' threshold for large boxes, is MINOR_DISCREPANCY (R1). Any other box or cell difference is a discrepancy.
verification_targets.published_values_source: Paper text, Fig. 4 (p. 6), visual; deposit Herskind&Riede_S3.xlsx (bigrams sheet) for cell PMI values

verification_targets.description: Map of the five Ertebølle-cluster motifs (C4, C5, C12, C13, D7): a coloured patch for the known extent of each motif, and 10 numbered pie charts (numbered as in Table 3) showing which of the five motifs each object carries. The Discussion (p. 6) reads it as C12 and C13 more eastern, C4, C5, and D7 more western.
verification_targets.comparison_method: No authors' code. Labelled verification aids (R1/Q5) do read-only lookups in `data`. For each Table 3 object they take its coordinates and which of the five motifs it carries (pie composition), plotted with ggplot2 geom_point under coord_quickmap(). For each motif they plot every S1 object carrying it (Coord.Long/Lat), then check visually that the published patch covers those objects and that the east/west reading holds. Scope: 10 pies (position + composition = 20 checks) plus 5 patches = 25 elements; element gate (7c). The patch construction method is unpublished. Shape differences that stem only from it are MINOR_DISCREPANCY (R1). If the patches turn out to rest on information outside S1, the patch elements are untestable under R2 and the target is recorded as partially verified (7c), counting against coverage. Credit only if PART 1 completes (Q6).
verification_targets.tolerance: Visual: pie positions and compositions must match (composition is an exact set); patch-coverage checks are visual. Basemap, projection, and legend artwork are not scored; unpublished patch-drawing conventions give MINOR_DISCREPANCY (R1).

verification_targets.display_item: Supplementary Information S3 (Herskind&Riede_S3.xlsx: bigrams, trigrams, quadrigrams sheets)
verification_targets.location: Zenodo record 10801706 v2, file Herskind&Riede_S3.xlsx (three sheets)
verification_targets.description: All bi-, tri-, and quadrigrams with observed frequency >= 3, sorted by PMI: tokens, token frequencies, observed frequency, expected frequency, and PMI. bigrams 165 rows x 7 columns, trigrams 106 x 9, quadrigrams 20 x 11.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Produced by PART 8 (S2.R lines 698-759; fwrite Bigrams.csv, Trigrams.csv, Quadrigrams.csv); the authors then imported these into Excel. compare.R reads the three S3 sheets (two header rows each) and aligns rows by token tuple. Tokens and integer frequencies are compared exactly; expected frequency and PMI are compared at the precision stored in the S3 cells. Row order (PMI descending) is checked separately. Scope: 2329 cells (1155 + 954 + 220); element gate 2329 (7c). Credit only if PARTs 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 complete (Q6; the bigram sheet rests on Part 7's subset, the trigram and quadrigram sheets on Part 6's recomputation). R4 log-base note as T02.
verification_targets.tolerance: Deterministic: tokens and integers EXACT_MATCH; expected frequency and PMI EXACT_MATCH or WITHIN_PRECISION (equal when rounded to the significant digits stored in the S3 cell, at most 15). Row-order differences confined to tied PMI values are MINOR_DISCREPANCY; any other difference is a discrepancy.
verification_targets.published_values_source: Deposited precomputed reference file Herskind&Riede_S3.xlsx (Zenodo v2, md5 812be5456d7e0e2adb97ecb5a975239e)

verification_targets.display_item: Named value: 483 ornamented objects in the corpus
verification_targets.location: p. 2, §2 ('a total of 483 objects'); p. 3, §2.1 ('the 483 ornamented artefacts are converted into ... equally as many ornamentation strings')
verification_targets.description: Corpus size: 483 objects, converted into 483 ornamentation strings.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Labelled verification aid (R1/Q5): nrow(data) from the PART 1 snapshot, and quanteda::ndoc(corpus) for the full-data corpus built in PART 3. S2.R never computes 483 (it hard-codes t <- 482 at line 86, explained in a comment as excluding one empty string). Scope: 1 value, checked twice; element gate 1. Credit only if PARTs 1 and 3 complete (Q6).

verification_targets.display_item: Named value: maximum of 15 individual motifs on a single object
verification_targets.description: 'the maximum number of individual motifs on a single object is 15', the stated basis for k = 13.
verification_targets.comparison_method: Labelled verification aid (R1/Q5), a documented quanteda call: max over documents of quanteda::ntype(quanteda::tokens(corpus)) on the PART 3 full-data corpus (primary, pre-stated). rules_applied.quotation: R3 Granularity: one target per display item. A multi-panel figure is one target, and its panels are described within it. Named values in the text are separate targets.
R4 Internal inconsistency: where the paper's text and its own tables or figures disagree, score against the stated value. Apply the PAPER_ERROR protocol if the reproduction disagrees, and escalate.

When a reproduced value disagrees with a published value, the reproduction is internally consistent, and the authors' own materials support the reproduced value, classify as PAPER_ERROR rather than MAJOR_DISCREPANCY. Admissible evidence, in descending strength: (1) the paper's own tabulated data; (2) the authors' deposited data for that analysis; (3) the authors' own code, run unmodified (invariant 2), on the authors' own data. The reproduction's own re-implementation is never evidence. The comparison report names the tier used. PAPER_ERROR findings escalate for human confirmation before entering study data.

Each target's verification method states its scope, which must equal the target's full published scope at the pre-stated tolerance. A check that covers part of a target is completed before the target counts as reproduced; otherwise the target is recorded as partially verified and counts against coverage. Where feasible, the plan declares the target's element count, and a deterministic gate compares it with the elements checked.

A wrapper may make an authors' statement error-tolerant only where the statement computes nothing that enters a result, such as registering a font; the tolerance is declared, and the run log records whether it fired. Per-section error capture is routine, but a target is credited only from a section that completed without error and whose inputs come only from sections that also completed. Sections may run in another order only when they are independent, none reading an object another defines; otherwise re-ordering changes the execution logic and is fail-and-uplift. A dependency fetched from a public repository is installed when the environment is built, pinned to a tagged release or, where the repository has none, to a recorded commit, preferring the one current at publication. An unpinned install at run time is not routine. Independence between sections is judged on every state a section can pass to another, namely named objects, files written and read, global options, and random-number state. The dependency sentence is read with the precedence rule above, so where the authors pinned the dependency, their pin is used.

Routine (execution environment): choosing among publicly available versions of dependencies and language runtimes, meaning releases from the package's official archive (for example CRAN or PyPI) or a tagged public repository, preferring the version current at publication. The search and the chosen versions are recorded. Fail-and-uplift: any edit to the authors' code that changes logic, indices, data selection, parameters, or the functions called, however obvious the intent. A deprecated function is handled by pinning a public version that still runs it; if none exists, replacing it is an edit, and so fail-and-uplift. A repaired result is recorded as uplift evidence and never counts toward coverage or the verdict.

A mechanical change made inside an authors' file rather than in a wrapper, such as a changed input path, breaks the wrapper rule even when it changes nothing computed. A result that rests on such a file does not count toward coverage or the verdict until it is re-run with the mechanics moved into a wrapper and the authors' file restored byte-identical. A change of logic, indices, data selection, parameters, or functions called remains fail-and-uplift whatever its effect, including a restructuring that gives the same result.
